title: What happens when a long Pi session compacts
description: A story of one compaction: memory flush, Haiku summary, decoration, fallback and exit compaction.

props.content: When a Pi session fills its context window, Pi replaces old messages with a summary. Iury's setup changes who writes that summary (Haiku 5.5), saves durable facts to memory first, and falls back to the session model if Haiku fails. **The least certain part: the design notes found no saved session where Haiku wrote a summary. Success is only seen in a test run.**

props.title: One compaction, start to finish
props.deck: Scroll to watch the pieces join in order.
props.takeaway: Facts are saved, then summarised, and a failure never blocks you.

props.caption: Two extensions listen to the same session_before_compact event.

beats.text: Context use crosses the threshold, you run `/compact`, or the window overflows. Those are the three reasons.
pi-optmem acts first. It removes its own wake messages from the input, then starts a detached worker that extracts up to 5 durable memory lines. Compaction does not wait for it.
compaction-model sends the same spans to Haiku with Pi's prompt, extra instructions and a 24K output budget.
If the model is missing, auth fails or the call errors, Pi uses the session model instead and you get a warning.
Either way the summary is wrapped and stored, and a card records what happened.

props.title: What gets added around Haiku's text
props.deck: The extension decorates the result. The model never writes these parts.
props.takeaway: The summary points back to the full evidence.

props.caption: Our own blocks are stripped from the model output first, so they are never duplicated.

items.title: Session start
items.body: First user message, verbatim, up to 2,000 characters.

items.title: Haiku's summary
items.body: Pi's structured sections plus extra notes.

items.title: Summary note
items.body: Reference only. Follow the latest message. Use session_query for exact wording.

props.content: The extra instructions ask Haiku to record approaches that failed and why, the last test or build result, unresolved error messages and stated preferences. Paths and identifiers stay verbatim.

props.title: Facts are saved before the old turns vanish
props.deck: A separate worker and a separate model call. No waiting.
props.takeaway: A short manual compaction is skipped: under about 1,000 tokens is not worth a call.

props.title: Guards
props.body: The worker rejects multiline, over-280-byte and recognisably sensitive lines. It skips facts already in the wake view and checks exact duplicates before each write. Semantic duplicates still depend on the model.

props.content: The wake view is added per request and never saved. Compaction therefore never summarises it, and it reloads on the next turn.

props.title: Fallback, failure and quitting
props.deck: Each path is visible in the session.
props.takeaway: A fallback costs one failed call and nothing more.

rows.title: Haiku cannot run
rows.body: Saved fallbacks said `No API provider registered for api: claude-code-cli`. A later commit routes compaction through the model registry.
rows.next: Confirm with a live automatic compaction.

rows.title: Input too big for 200K
rows.body: Observed maximum was about 167K tokens (an estimate). Tool-call arguments are a third of the input and are never truncated.
rows.next: A fit check and argument masking are planned, not built.

rows.title: Summary too short
rows.body: One test gave a 467-token summary from 45K tokens of input.
rows.next: Report summary length beside quality scores in the planned evaluation.

rows.title: Fallback
rows.body: A card is recorded and a warning shows if there is a UI.

rows.title: Failed compaction
rows.body: A `failed` entry records the reason. Aborts are not reported.

rows.title: Quit with a big context
rows.body: With `compactOnExitMinTokens` set, a detached RPC process compacts the closed session behind a lock file, with a 10-minute timeout. Reopening early shows a warning.

props.title: Things the plan rejected
props.deck: Pi or existing tools already cover them.

props.content:
- Clearing stale tool output in normal context. It breaks the prompt cache.
- Re-injecting `AGENTS.md`. It lives in the system prompt and survives compaction.
- Re-injecting files or todos, or building a new handoff system.
